expectations.text: Refuses to set a numeric engagement-rate target for this channel.
expectations.evidence: 'Don't commit to a 4-6% engagement rate'.

expectations.text: Refuses to set a follower-count target to reach by doors.
expectations.evidence: 'A follower-by-doors figure would be invented.'

expectations.text: Gives the reason for the refusal: such a threshold is false precision imported from an unrelated domain, and the reader would optimise against a number that means nothing here.
expectations.evidence: 'Importing it would be false precision from an unrelated domain.'

expectations.text: Declines the 4-6% engagement benchmark specifically rather than adopting or adjusting it.
expectations.evidence: 'The 4-6% benchmark has no stated source or definition.'

expectations.text: Substitutes four self-set measures: every dated post shipped on its date, a per-platform tracked link, amplification take-up, and the archive produced.
expectations.evidence: Items 1-5 cover dated posts, per-platform tracked links, take-up and the archive, plus the personal-account comparison.

expectations.text: Flags 'every dated post shipped on its date' as binary, fully inside the organiser's control, and the measure that fails most often on volunteer teams.
expectations.evidence: 'the one measure fully in your control, and the one volunteer teams miss most'; 'checked yes or no'.

expectations.text: States that per-platform tracked links must be decided before launch because they cannot be added retroactively.
expectations.evidence: 'in place before the first post... They can't be added retroactively.'

expectations.text: States that reading the tracked links belongs to the marketing plan while creating them belongs to the social channel.
expectations.evidence: 'The marketing plan reads them and you create them.'

expectations.text: Presents any published event-account engagement figure it cites as descriptive of the accounts measured, never as a threshold to hit.
expectations.evidence: 'They describe that audience, not a threshold for you.'

expectations.text: States that established conference accounts accumulate followers across recurring editions while a campaign account starts near-cold each edition, so follower-based benchmarks do not transfer.
expectations.evidence: 'Event accounts also start near-cold each cycle'; the established brands were 'built over up to 14 editions'.
